track: 20-39: Complex supplier: improve one specific circuit, frame schedule, decoder, or paid recursive profile

candidate_tasks_evaluated.title: Partial E4 -> E5 entrance-promotion reversion inside one 4-helper group [659, 661, 662, 663] of U8 to fill T37 rank-1 idle gaps
candidate_tasks_evaluated.summary: Reverting m in {1, 2, 3} helpers of [659, 661, 662, 663] from E5 (dim 5) to E4 (dim 4) forces the 12 bipartite delivery gates B[420..431] into {656, 657, 658, 660} to split between frames E4 and E5, splitting the single rank-4 climb (1 -> 5) on {656, 657, 658, 660} into (1 -> 4 -> 5) and yielding local profile deltas {1:+2, 2:+1, 3:+3, 4:-3} (m=1) and {1:+2, 2:+2, 3:+4, 4:-4} (m=2), which strictly worsen the complex moment.

candidate_tasks_evaluated.title: Frame-0 premix refactorization at the head of section A in U8
candidate_tasks_evaluated.summary: The frame-0 premix prefix of section A in U8 comprises only 57 scalar macros (482 real primitives per orientation) with small coefficients (max_num = 2, max_den = 2), offering negligible circuit savings.

candidate_tasks_evaluated.title: Two-sided Markowitz LPR (R^{-1} P L^{-1}) Schur-complement refactorization with Weyl-group signed cycles for full_frame_cleanup on the selected U8 complex supplier word
candidate_tasks_evaluated.summary: Replaces the 6,105-macro one-sided dyadic Gauss-Jordan high_inverse in U8 full_frame_cleanup with a 3,525-macro two-sided Markowitz R^{-1} P L^{-1} factorization with Weyl-group signed cycles (seed=30, trial=16, swap_pen=6, scale_pen=0), cutting cleanup macros by 2,580 (-42.26%), cleanup real primitives by 37,320 per orientation (-54.31%, or -74,640 across the forward+backward pair), maximum cleanup numerator from 131,646 to 8, and backward prefix L1 bit bound from 72 bits to 54 bits (-18 bits, 210,704x reduction) while preserving all 728 exact columns, native frames, paid recursive profile, and residual adapter recipes.
